newsitem.title: USA: Swedish envoy to see detained American in N.Korea.
newsitem.headline: Swedish envoy to see detained American in N.Korea.

text.p: An American citizen being detained in North Korea on espionage charges will get a visit on Friday from a Swedish envoy acting in the interest of the U.S. government, the State Department said on Thursday.
State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said diplomat Ake Lovquist from Sweden, which represents U.S. interests in North Korea, had previously visited the American on Sept. 17.

Burns thanked Sweden for "excellent work" in the case and repeated U.S. calls for the immediate release of the detainee, identified in U.S. media reports as Evan Carl Hunziker. North Korea spells the surname Hunzike. The State Department has declined to release his name.

"We hope and trust that the American citizen is in good health, is being given the proper care and treatment that he deserves under international law and regulations," Burns said. "And we hope that the North Korean government will elect to release him immediately."

Hunziker was arrested on Aug. 24 after crossing from China. North Korea's state news agency said it had been "proved by investigation" that he was a spy for South Korea and he would have to "take appropriate penal responsibility."

Burns did not say where Hunziker was being held but noted that reports from Lovquist's visit might be delayed, given communications difficulties in North Korea and the fact that the diplomat would have to take a four-hour train trip from Pyongyang to see the American.

Burns said Lovquist would ask pertinent questions about North Korea's treatment, adding that "Given the state of North Korea's legal system and given the nature of the government we're not at all confident that he would receive a fair trial, should ... this case be brought to trial."

Hunziker's father, Edwin, has described his son as a divorced 26-year-old who has drifted around Alaska and Washington state working on crab boats and doing odd jobs, according to the Washington Post.

Hunziker said his son became an evangelical Christian while serving a jail sentence in Alaska last year for drunk driving. Other family members were quoted as saying Hunziker went to do Christian missionary work in South Korea.

At 6 feet 3 inches (1.9 metres) tall and more than 200 pounds (91 kg), with the build and complexion of his Swedish-American father, Hunziker "doesn't look Asian," the Post said. Hunziker's mother is a Korean native but he speaks only a few words of Korean, the newspaper reported.

U.S. Assistant Secretary of State Winston Lord was in South Korea on Thurday to reassure the Seoul government of Washington's concern over recent North Korean actions, notably the infiltration into South Korea of 26 North Koreans from a stranded submarine last month.

Lord's arrival for a three-day visit coincided with a massive manhunt by thousands of troops in rugged east coast woodlands for North Korean agents suspected of strangling an elderly woman and shooting dead two South Korean men.
